speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me if this started suddenly after an injury or has been developing gradually over time? Also, is there any redness, warmth, or a visible lump on the affected finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Gamekeeper's thumb (chronic ulnar collateral ligament injury of the thumb) is unlikely given the location (ring finger) and mechanism. Based on the traumatic mechanism (jersey pull) and acute onset (2 days ago) with swelling and pain, the most likely diagnosis is an acute ligamentous injury or fracture of the right ring finger, specifically involving the PIP or MCP joint. I need to confirm the exact location of maximal tenderness and check for joint instability. REQUEST TEST: X-ray of the right hand.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
